svg.aria-label: QBM-02 · Photosynthetic electron transport and plastid redox
svg.text: QBM-02 · Photosynthetic electron transport and plastid redox
Magnetically addressable nodes of the chloroplast, from water oxidation to NADPH, with the evidence tier for each

g.title: H2O tier T4 (verified) quantum class: structural_context

Plastocyanin (PETE1/2) tier T3 (inferred) quantum class: spin_relaxation_modulated nuclei: 1H AGI: AT1G76100, AT1G20340 rationale: A mononuclear Cu(II)/Cu(I) centre performing one-electron transfer, so formally paramagnetic in the oxidised state.
caveat: Deliberately classed as spin_relaxation_modulated rather than as a radical-pair partner. A single copper centre relaxes fast and has no correlated partner, so coherent singlet-triplet mixing is not available here; only a relaxation-based effect could be argued, and none has been shown.

Photosystem II tier T3 (inferred) quantum class: semiquinone_radical, ros_leak_site nuclei: 1H AGI: ATCG00020, AT1G06680 rationale: The QA/QB sites hold a kinetically stabilised plastosemiquinone, and PSII is a major singlet-oxygen source under excess light. Both are one-electron chemistry in a defined pocket, which is the setting a radical-pair argument needs.
caveat: PSII's dominant ROS species is singlet oxygen from the P680 triplet, not superoxide. Triplet chlorophyll formation is itself spin chemistry, so a field effect here would be more plausible than at most nodes — but it is also a route the review does not develop, and no measurement exists.
Plastoquinone pool (PQ / PQH2) tier T4 (verified) quantum class: structural_context

Plastosemiquinone (PQ·−) tier T3 (inferred) quantum class: semiquinone_radical, radical_pair_donor, ros_leak_site nuclei: 1H rationale: The plastid counterpart of ubisemiquinone, and the same argument applies: a protein-bound organic radical with a measurable lifetime is the most credible site for field-dependent branching in the chain.

Cytochrome b6f Rieske [2Fe-2S] (PETC) tier T3 (inferred) quantum class: rieske_2Fe2S, semiquinone_radical nuclei: 57Fe, 33S, 1H AGI: AT4G03280 rationale: Structurally and mechanistically the plastid twin of the mitochondrial Rieske centre (QBO:RIESKE_FES), with the same bifurcated Q-cycle chemistry. The review treats both as the same class of candidate target.

Cytochrome b6 / f hemes (PETA, PETB) tier T3 (inferred) quantum class: heme_electron_carrier nuclei: 57Fe, 1H AGI: ATCG00540, ATCG00720 rationale: One-electron heme carriers, paramagnetic in the ferric state, adjacent to the semiquinone-generating Q cycle.
Cyclic electron flow (PGR5 / PGRL1) tier T4 (inferred) quantum class: structural_context AGI: AT2G05620, AT4G22890

Photosystem I Fe/S centres (FX, FA, FB) tier T2 (reported) quantum class: iron_sulfur_4Fe4S, radical_pair_acceptor, triplet_yield_sensitive nuclei: 57Fe, 33S, 1H AGI: ATCG01060 Parmagnani2023: The geomagnetic field is required for normal lima bean photosynthesis, PSI/LHCI content and ROS production; near-null field conditions altered photosynthetic electron transport. [10.3390/ijms24032896] rationale: PSI is the strongest structural case in the whole atlas. Charge separation at P700 produces a genuine spin-correlated radical pair (P700·+ A1·−), which is the textbook example of the species the radical-pair mechanism describes — it is studied by exactly that formalism in photosynthesis spectroscopy. Three [4Fe-4S] clusters then carry the electron onward.
caveat: The P700·+ A1·− pair is extremely short-lived, and the well-characterised magnetic-field effects on it are seen in isolated preparations at fields far above geomagnetic. Structural plausibility is high; relevance at 50 uT is not established.
Thylakoid ATP synthase tier T4 (inferred) quantum class: structural_context AGI: AT4G04640

Ferredoxin (FD1, FD2) tier T2 (reported) quantum class: iron_sulfur_2Fe2S nuclei: 57Fe, 33S AGI: AT1G10960, AT1G60950 Vigani2021: Geomagnetic field conditions modulate iron-sulfur interplay in Arabidopsis, particularly under combined iron and sulfur deficiency. [10.3390/ijms221810166] rationale: The distribution hub of plastid reducing power. A perturbation here reaches carbon fixation, nitrogen and sulfur assimilation and redox regulation at once, which is why the review nominates ferredoxin biogenesis specifically.

Ferredoxin-NADP+ reductase (FNR1, FNR2) tier T3 (inferred) quantum class: flavin_semiquinone, ros_leak_site nuclei: 1H, 14N AGI: AT5G66190, AT1G20020 rationale: FNR necessarily transits a flavin semiquinone: it is the step that converts one-electron chemistry into two-electron chemistry, so a half-reduced flavin is obligatory rather than incidental. That makes it the plastid's clearest analogue of the cryptochrome flavin.
NADPH / NADP+ tier T4 (verified) quantum class: structural_context

Plastid superoxide / H2O2 tier T2 (reported) quantum class: ros_leak_site AGI: AT4G25100, AT2G28190 Parmagnani2023: Reactive oxygen species production differed between geomagnetic and near-null field conditions in lima bean. [10.3390/ijms24032896] Parmagnani2022: Near-null magnetic field alters ROS-associated transcriptomic and metabolomic programmes in Arabidopsis. [10.3390/biom12121824] rationale: As in the mitochondrion, the amplifier rather than the mechanism: threshold behaviour converts a small change in electron branching into a signal.

svg.text: The photosynthetic chain redrawn with each node's quantum chemistry and the evidence behind it. Photosystem I is the
strongest structural case in the atlas: charge separation at P700 makes a genuine spin-correlated radical pair, the species the
radical-pair mechanism was written for. It is nevertheless only T2, because the one direct field measurement on photosynthesis
in the review's bibliography was made in lima bean rather than Arabidopsis, and because that pair is extremely short-lived and
its known field effects are seen well above geomagnetic strength. Cyclic electron flow is drawn for the same reason alternative
oxidase appears on QBM-01 — it lets a chloroplast rebalance ATP against NADPH without changing linear flux, so measuring
linear electron transport alone cannot separate "no effect" from "compensated effect". Four nodes are plastid-encoded (ATCG
loci) and will receive no value from poly-A-selected RNA-seq, which is most of OSDR's plant studies. Derived from: Figures 1B and
5 of Porterfield & Barker, "Plant Responses to Near-Null Magnetic Fields" — expanded to gene level and bound to Arabidopsis loci.
Node counts by evidence tier: T2=3, T3=6, T4=5. Schematic topology only — no quantitative value is encoded in this base map;
numbers appear only when measured data is projected onto it.
